I tried growing years ago. Norther Lights 5. Should have been difficult to fuck up. I fucked up. I'm really good with germinating and cloning and getting them up to the flowering stage, but it's the flowering stage I fuck up. Probably shouldn't have used soil and gone full hydro.

I use a hybrid method. Fox Farm's Ocean Forest, 4 to 5 inches of large perlite in the bottom of 20 gallon square bins. Drill out a couple dozen holes in the sides and floor of the bins first, 1/2 inch. Then mix 1/3 perlite with 2/3rd soil. Then top off with another 1 to 2 inches of perlite. Elevate the bins, with catchment basins for water runoff. You want to do something similar but much smaller with the seedlings, and keep them covered with saran wrap until they get to the 3rd node, before transplanting to the bins.

Fox Farm comes a little pre-aged, but I've had best results storing them for an additional 6 to 9 months to ensure the microcritters are superactive.

I tilt the LEDs to create a minidome around the plants for full coverage, wind up with a lollipop super sticky canopy. 2 to 3 inches from the buds. LEDs run cool, but you still have to run a swivel fan to keep the outer canopy from getting too hot. Sometimes I have to adjust the lights 3 to 4 times a day.

Come flower time, run super dry humid air -- 10% to 20%, except right after watering. I cut the watering down to 3 days per week for the first couple in the flower cycle, then 2 days for 4 to 5 weeks, then once every 5 days for the final weeks. That last week, as you probably know, is the critical period where you need the microscope to see if the trikes are ripe.
